name: Notion

steps.d: Open the Developer portal and create a new public connection.

steps.t: Set the redirect URI and scope
steps.d: Enter your redirect URI under the OAuth configuration section and choose Any workspace or Selected workspaces only. You can't change the scope later.

steps.t: Copy your client ID and secret
steps.d: Find them in the connection's Configuration tab, and keep them out of source code.

steps.t: Send users to the authorization URL
steps.d: Link users to the authorization URL from the Developer portal. Notion then redirects them to your redirect URI with a code.

blockers.s: Notion's docs say the Authorization URL field fills in after a public connection is submitted for review.

checklist.answer: Open the Developer portal and create a new public connection.
Notion has internal connections, personal access tokens and public connections. Only public connections use OAuth 2.0, so other people can install them.
The form takes your connection details, your redirect URIs and an installation scope, either Any workspace or Selected workspaces only. The scope can't be changed after creation.
The redirect URI is where users are sent after they authorize the connection. You enter it under the OAuth configuration section.
Find the connection's secrets in the Configuration tab of the Developer portal, and keep them out of source code.
Access is granted per page: users pick which workspace pages to share when they authorize the connection.
Public connections must go through a Notion security review before they're listed on the Marketplace. You can create and use one without listing it.
“After submission, expect to hear back from our team within 5-10 business days via email.”
Listings are rejected for reasons that range from brand or trademark issues to quality concerns, or when the baseline criteria aren't met.
